title: Memorial Day Cannabis Ideas for the Start of Summer
h1: Kick Off Summer: Cannabis Ideas for Memorial Day Weekend

body:
Memorial Day cannabis plans work best when they're simple. Think a private backyard or cottage, a few easy formats, clearly labeled food and a plan for getting everyone home safely. Below you'll find format picks for a cookout, profiles matched to summer moments, hosting basics and a link to our infused BBQ sauce.

## Why Memorial Day weekend feels like summer's start

Memorial Day, on the last Monday in May, honors the men and women who died serving in the U.S. armed forces. It's worth a pause before the grill gets going. The next one falls on May 31, 2027.

For many Michiganders, the long weekend is also the unofficial start of summer. Cottages open, docks go in and the first backyard cookouts of the year get underway.

If cannabis is part of your weekend, plan it for private property. Michigan doesn't allow consumption in public places, and owners can set their own rules for their property, so ask before you light up at a rental or a friend's place.

## Memorial Day cannabis: format picks for a cookout

| Format | Why it works at a cookout | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|
| Edibles | No smoke, easy to portion | A slow start, 30 to 60 minutes or more |
| Drinks | Something to sip, in measured servings | How many servings are in each can or bottle |
| Pre-rolls | Easy to share among adults 21+ | Drifting smoke; pick a spot away from non-smokers |
| Vapes | Less lingering smell | Still consumption, so private property only |
| Tinctures | Measured drops that can go in food or drink | Timing varies, so wait before taking more |

Cannabis drinks are a newer option for a party. They give guests something to hold, and Michigan caps a serving at 10 mg of THC, as of October 2026. Never mix them with alcohol, and if you're weighing the two, read our comparison of [THC drinks and alcohol](/blog/thc-drinks-vs-alcohol/).

Tinctures are flexible: a measured dropper can go under the tongue or into a drink or dish. Our [cannabis tincture guide](/blog/cannabis-tincture-guide/) explains how they work and how to measure them.

Shopping ahead? Browse your store's menu on our [shop page](/shop/) and order ahead for pickup, and check your store's hours before the long weekend. For a packing list by format, see our [summer cannabis kit builder](/blog/summer-cannabis-kit-builder/).

## Infused food basics: cannabutter, oils and dosing guests safely

Cooking with cannabis starts with an infused fat, usually butter or oil, and our [cannabutter guide](/blog/canna-butter/) walks through it step by step. The harder part is dosing, because homemade infusions are estimates.

Here's the math, and why it's only a starting point. Say you infuse 3.5 grams of flower labeled 20% total THC. That's 3,500 mg times 0.20, or about 700 mg of THC on paper. Some of it is lost during decarboxylation, the heating step that activates THC, and more during infusion, so the real amount is lower and hard to pin down.

Now divide it up. If all that butter goes into 24 cookies, the paper math says up to about 29 mg per cookie, nearly three times Michigan's 10 mg retail serving. That's too strong for most guests. Use less flower, make more portions or cut smaller pieces to bring the estimate down.

- Mix thoroughly, since an infusion can spread unevenly through a batch.
- Tell guests the estimated amount per piece, and suggest they start with half.
- Remind everyone that eaten cannabis can take 30 to 60 minutes to start and around 1.5 to 3 hours to peak.
- For a crowd, labeled store-bought edibles take the guesswork out of it.

## Strain profiles for summer moments

Instead of chasing strain names, think in profiles. Terpenes, the aroma compounds in cannabis, give each strain its scent, and labels or menus sometimes list the leading ones. Effects differ from one person to the next, so take these as starting points.

| Moment | Profile people often reach for | Format idea |
|---|---|---|
| Backyard picnic | Bright and citrusy (limonene-forward) | Low-dose edibles or a cannabis drink |
| Grilling | Peppery and spicy (caryophyllene-forward) | A pre-roll once the food is off the grill |
| Garden afternoon | Fresh and piney (pinene-forward) | A tincture or a low-dose gummy |
| Backyard party | Sweet and fruity | Single-serve drinks or pre-rolls to share |
| Bonfire | Earthy and woodsy (myrcene-forward) | Flower or a pre-roll |
| Stargazing | Floral and mellow (linalool-forward) | A small puff from a vape |

A strain name is a loose guide. The label's numbers, and the terpene list when there is one, tell you more. Start low with anything new.

## Hosting responsibly: labels, 21+ only, infused food kept apart, rides home

- **21 and older only.** Only guests 21 and older should partake, and no one should feel pressured to.
- **Label everything.** Mark infused dishes, sauces and drinks clearly, with the estimated THC per serving.
- **Keep infused food apart.** Give it its own table or cooler, away from the regular food and well out of reach of kids and pets. Poison center reports of young children eating cannabis edibles climbed from 207 in 2017 to 3,054 in 2021, nearly all of them in homes.
- **Make sober the default.** Put plenty of regular food and non-infused drinks out, and let guests opt in.
- **Skip the mix.** Keep alcohol and cannabis separate.
- **Plan rides home.** Driving while impaired by cannabis is against Michigan law. Line up sober drivers or rides, or invite people to stay over.
- **Know the number.** The National Poison Control Center, 1-800-222-1222, is printed on every Michigan cannabis label.

## Recipe: an infused sweet-and-smoky BBQ sauce

If you want one infused item on the table, make it a sauce. Guests decide how much to add, and the regular sauce can sit right beside it. Our [infused sweet-and-smoky BBQ sauce recipe](/blog/sweet-and-smokey-bbq-sauce/) walks through the cooking and the dosing math.

A few habits keep it party-safe. Serve the infused sauce on the side instead of brushing it on everything. Label the bottle with the estimated THC per tablespoon, and keep it far from the kids' table.

faq.q: How do I host a cannabis-friendly cookout?
faq.a: Start with private property where cannabis is allowed, and keep it to adults 21 and older for anyone partaking. Offer a few easy formats, label every infused item with its estimated THC per serving, and keep those items apart from the regular food. Make non-infused options the default, skip alcohol pairings and line up sober rides home before the first burger hits the grill.

faq.q: How should infused food be dosed for guests?
faq.a: Low and clearly. Work out the estimated THC per piece, remember that homemade numbers are uncertain, and keep each piece at or below Michigan's 10 mg retail serving. Tell guests the estimate, suggest a half portion to start and remind them that eaten cannabis builds slowly over the first couple of hours. For a crowd, labeled store-bought edibles are the simplest choice.

faq.q: Which strain profiles fit summer gatherings?
faq.a: Many people match aroma to the moment: bright citrus profiles for daytime picnics, peppery or piney ones around the grill, and earthy profiles once the bonfire is going. Everyone responds a little differently, so use those pairings as starting points. Look past the strain name to the numbers on the label and any terpene list, and start low with anything new.

faq.q: Are cannabis drinks a good fit for a party?
faq.a: They can be. Drinks give guests something to sip and come in measured servings, with Michigan capping each serving at 10 mg of THC. They work like edibles, so effects take a while to arrive. Check whether a can holds one serving or several, pace yourself, keep them apart from regular drinks and never mix them with alcohol.

claims.claim: Order ahead for pickup 'so you're not waiting in line on a holiday Saturday'
claims.fix: Assumed stores are open and busy on holiday weekends. High Society publishes no holiday hours. Now: order ahead for pickup and check your store's hours before the long weekend.

claims.claim: Dosing math: 3.5 g x 20% = about 700 mg on paper; / 24 cookies = about 29 mg, nearly three times a 10 mg serving; decarboxylation and infusion losses make it an estimate
claims.source: Arithmetic (3,500 x 0.20 = 700; 700 / 24 = 29.17; 2.9x); framed as an estimate per the recipe rule

claims.source: General aroma descriptions; presented as profiles people reach for, with no effect claims.

claims.fix: 'at home' tightened to 'in homes' (the study says 'residential setting', which includes other people's homes).
